business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-Speed Dipping Production of Powder-Free Synthetic Nitrile Gloves

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Estado Español; unitary national jurisdiction; Central Commercial Registry seated in Madrid)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European codified system; unitary state with autonomous communities; direct application of EU law, including Regulation (EU) 2017/745 on medical devices)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EU-Mexico Global Agreement (Economic Partnership, Political Coordination and Cooperation Agreement, in force for trade since 2001; modernization process ongoing)
Agreement between the Kingdom of Spain and the United Mexican States for the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (2006, in force)
Spain-Argentina Bilateral Investment Treaty for the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (in force)
Spain-Chile Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force, with investor-State arbitration)
Spain-Colombia and Spain-Peru Bilateral Investment Treaties (in force)

Comprehensive DTAAs with the United States, China, the United Kingdom and the EU/EEA member states, with investment protection framed under the EU common commercial policy and the EU investment agreement portfolio for Latin American partners

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (in particular Articles 4, 14 and 32, as amended by Real Decreto-ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril, transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, approving the implementing Regulation of Ley 10/2010; Regulation (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2018/843; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Ley de Sociedades de Capital, Articles 9-13 on registered office and transparency of ultimate ownership; Real Decreto-ley 7/2021 establishing the Registro de Titularidad Real operated by the Colegio de Registradores under the Ministry of Justice; Circular SEPBLAC 1/2022 on client due diligence and beneficial ownership reporting.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (SEPBLAC, AEAT, judicial and police authorities, notaries and obliged institutions with a demonstrable AML need-to-know; not a fully public register)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Valid passport or national identity card of each founder, director and statutory agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent civil authority or national police/civil registry authority of the country of origin of each individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) issued by the competent apostille authority of the country of origin, followed by sworn Spanish translation (traducción jurada) before a Spanish Public Notary; consular legalization at the Spanish Consulate is required for documents originating from non-Hague member states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record (certificado de antecedentes penales) for each director; for Spanish residents, the Certificate of the Registro Central de Penados
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or General Prosecutor's Office of the country of origin; within Spain, Registro Central de Penados of the Ministry of Justice (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus sworn Spanish translation for non-EU/EEA origin; for EU/EEA documents, the certificate is verified via the electronic criminal records exchange (BISIS) and, where the receiving notary so decides, certified by sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, status and good standing of any non-resident legal entity that will appear as shareholder and as disclosed UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry, company registrar or Chamber of Commerce of the jurisdiction of the shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the competent authority of the state of origin, accompanied by sworn Spanish translation of the extract; where the origin state is not a Hague member, consular legalization through the Spanish Consulate is mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and source-of-funds commitment letter covering the initial capital contribution and the pre-incorporation financing plan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution of the founding party, executed by its Money Laundering Reporting Officer or equivalent compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature notarized in the jurisdiction of issuance with an apostille; for non-Hague origin jurisdictions, consular legalization of the notarial chain; alternatively, a certified bank SWIFT reference may be accepted after SEPBLAC-standard KYC validation by the receiving Spanish entity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of every UBO, director, attorney-in-fact and authorized signatory against: (i) SEPBLAC/SEPD prohibition list; (ii) EU Council consolidated financial sanctions list (CFSP) and Spanish restrictive-measures regulations; (iii) United Nations Security Council consolidated list; (iv) OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists (required by Spanish bank practice where USD clearing or a US nexus is anticipated); and (v) international PEP databases derived from FATF and Global-PEP standards, supplemented by continuous adverse-media searches. The protocol requires an automated and human dual-screening flow with complete audit trail retention for a minimum of ten years pursuant to Article 25 Ley 10/2010; any positive or inconclusive match triggers enhanced due diligence, independent review and escalation to the Compliance Committee before incorporation proceeds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) of Spain - electronic application filed through the RMC e-Office (www.rmc.es) or via the notarial corporate gateway CIRCE (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas); the approved outcome is the 'certificado negativo de denominación social' issued by the RMC
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The requested company denomination must be rendered in Spanish script using Latin characters; co-official Iberian languages (Catalan/Valencian, Basque and Galician) and Latin-script foreign-language names are admissible where the statutory deed and sworn translation so reflect, and the denomination must be reproduced character-for-character in the notarial deed and the RMC certificate. Accents, punctuation and spacing must coincide exactly with the reserved name; numerals must be written in words; the suffix 'S.L.' or 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' is mandatory and forms part of the reserved denomination. The RMC will reject names that are identical, phonetically similar or visually almost identical to an existing registered denomination, and will apply the controlled-token rules set out in Article 7 of the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Real Decreto 1597/1989).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate reserves the exact denomination for 180 days from issuance and is non-extendable. If the incorporation deed is not registered within that period, the founder must file a new RMC name-application and pay the official fee again. Upon refusal, the RMC issues a reasoned certification of coincidence or inadmissibility. The applicant may (i) request reconsideration before the RMC within ten business days, (ii) file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) against the refusal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministry of Justice within one month of notification, and (iii) if the administrative remedy is dismissed, pursue judicial review in the contencioso-administrativo jurisdiction through the Juzgado Central de lo Contencioso-Administrativo with subsequent recourse to the Audiencia Nacional. All appeal steps are processed digitally through the Ministry of Justice e-Office and require representation by a lawyer of the founding party.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole statutory registered office. Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital requires the SL to declare a registered office situated in Spain at the place of effective administration or principal activity. For ISIC 3250 sterile nitrile glove production, the medical-device regulatory regime under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 and Real Decreto 192/2023, de 21 de marzo, additionally requires a physical production, sterilisation and warehousing facility in Spain and custody of the CE technical documentation at a tangible local address. Serviced-office or virtual addresses may be used only for auxiliary commercial or back-office functions and cannot lawfully replace the statutory and tax-fiscal domicile declared in the deed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High risk: 65-75% probability of an unannounced physical inspection by the Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios (AEMPS) or the Notified Body within the first 12 months of sterile-class certification; AEAT and SEPBLAC on-site scrutiny of newly incorporated SL structures is estimated at 35-45% during the same period.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance application and issuance of the negative denomination certificate (certificado negativo de denominación social)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official RMC statutory tariff under the Order of 30 November 1991 (amount approximately EUR 36.50)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Execution of the incorporation deed (escritura de constitución) before a Spanish Public Notary, including standard Articles of Association and appointment of directors
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public of the chosen Spanish notarial district (Madrid or Barcelona)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial fee scale for deed-of-incorporation transactions with a nominal capital band customary for SL formation (EUR 650-720 where the full-payment EUR 3,000 capital route is chosen; lower nominal capital under Ley 18/2022 attracts a proportionally reduced fee)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation (traducción jurada) of three foreign-origin corporate and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Traductor Jurado appointed under the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs procedure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing professional market tariff of USD 55-70 per certified document, fixed in the translation engagement letter

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille legalization of three foreign-origin documents (passports, criminal records, corporate good-standing extract)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of each country of origin (Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Ministry of Justice, as applicable under the 1961 Hague Convention)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule of the issuing state, estimated at USD 50-60 per apostille; additional postal and courier charges included

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Provisional and definitive Tax Identification Number (NIF) application to the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and the acting tax assistance agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory nil AEAT filing charge; nominal professional handling fee of approximately USD 40 for the CIF provisional code and subsequent notification to the registry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the SL in the Provincial Mercantile Registry of the registered office seat
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registration tariff of the Colegio de Registradores based on the face value of the share capital and the number of statutory pages (estimated EUR 190-210)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing of the beneficial ownership declaration in the Registro de Titularidad Real and set-up of the AML/CFT client file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Colegio de Registradores / obliged entity compliance function for retailing the UBO statement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official register processing fee (approximately USD 50) plus professional preparation and consistency verification of the UBO structure at the prevailing compliance-services market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: External counsel due diligence, PEP/OFAC/UN sanctions screening, UBO verification and pre-incorporation advisory (fixed fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External legal and AML compliance firm engaged by the founders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee for a low-risk-standard medical consumables manufacturing SL, inclusive of automated and manual screening, adverse-media analysis and report completeness

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation and physical reception services for the first three months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered office domiciliation service provider in Madrid or Barcelona
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of USD 130-160 per month for corporate domiciliation with physical mail reception and stated address availability

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account pre-approval, KYC documentation set and compliance interview facilitation with the target banking institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate services agent and bank compliance department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank administrative and compliance charging benchmark of approximately USD 80-110 for pre-account opening KYC handling

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Spanish Companies Act), Articles 19-22 (Incorporation), 58-60 (SL minimum capital), 62-63 (Payment of capital), 133-162 (Administration bodies), and 209-234 (Annual accounts); supplemented by the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Royal Decree 1784/1996)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) for the negative name certificate; Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office for the definitive inscription; incorporation deed executed before a Spanish Notary
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (notarial public deed of incorporation) filed with the Registro Mercantil and inscribed in the hoja registral de la sociedad
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada requires minimum share capital of EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,240), fully subscribed and fully paid up at incorporation in cash or in-kind; payment must be evidenced by a bank deposit certificate issued in the name of the company-in-formation; no statutory escrow account is required, but the bank certificate is attached to the notarial protocol and any withdrawal of the capital before registration requires prior authorization of the Registro Mercantil
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION - RESOLVED: (1) Each founding member subscribes the Participaciones Sociales set opposite his or her name, representing the share capital of EUR 3,000, the minimum statutory capital, fully paid as evidenced by the bank deposit certificate annexed. (2) The registered office is adopted at Calle ..., Madrid, Spain. (3) The management body is entrusted to Mr/Ms [Name] as Sole Administrator, who accepts the office by signature, with all legal and statutory powers. (4) The Administrator is authorized to obtain the provisional NIF, execute the public deed, register the Company in the Commercial Registry, legalize corporate books and perform all ancillary formalities. (5) The corporate books - minutes book and partners register - are opened and submitted for legalization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and certificate of no prior conflicting denomination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central via the online platform of the Colegio de Registradores de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an electronic application for a negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación social), proposing up to three alternative company names in order of preference; the Central Registry verifies that no identical or confusingly similar denomination is already registered; pay the statutory fee electronically; the certificate is issued digitally with a validity of three months (renewable for an additional three months) and must be delivered to the Notary at the deed execution stage.
required_dossiers: DNI, NIE or passport of each founding member
Signed application form for denomination certification
Electronic proof of payment of the official fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first proposed name is refused due to conflict or similarity, the second and third alternatives are automatically considered; if all proposed names are rejected, a new application may be filed; a refusal may be appealed before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública within the applicable statutory term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the corporate bank account and deposit of the minimum share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution authorized by the Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a company-in-formation account in the name of the future entity with a Spanish bank; deposit the full amount of EUR 3,000 by cash or wire transfer; the bank must issue a certificate of deposit (certificado de desembolso) stating the depositor, the amount, the account number and the date; deliver the original certificate to the Notary for attachment to the public deed.
required_dossiers: Valid negative name certificate
Draft bylaws (estatutos sociales) of the company
Passports or NIEs of all shareholders
Bank AML/KYC information: source of funds, business plan, and beneficial ownership declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank holds the account opening for enhanced AML due diligence, provide comprehensive source-of-funds documentation and corporate structure details; if the deposit certificate contains any error, request a rectified certificate from the bank at no cost before the notarial appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the public deed of incorporation before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (Notaría) located in the territory of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Attend the notarial appointment with all founders and the appointed administrator; the Notary verifies the legal capacity of the parties, the validity of the name certificate, the bank deposit certificate, and the lawfulness of the drafted bylaws; the deed is read and signed by the Notary and all shareholders; immediately after signature, the Notary electronically requests the provisional NIF from AEAT and delivers certified copies to the parties.
required_dossiers: Certificación negativa de denominación social
Bank deposit certificate of the EUR 3,000 capital
Articles of Association (estatutos) signed by all founders
Passports or NIEs of all shareholders
Pre-completed Modelo 036 census application
Affidavit or certificate of good standing for the appointed administrator when required by the Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary refuses execution because of a defect in the bylaws or documentation, amend the deficient clauses and reconvene; missing or expired documents may be substituted and the appointment rescheduled without invalidating the intended incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the provisional Tax Identification Number (NIF provisional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Delegación competente in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Notary submits the provisional NIF application electronically to AEAT within twenty-four hours of deed execution, attaching a certified electronic copy of the deed and the completed census data; AEAT issues the provisional NIF certificate with the company's letter-based tax code; this provisional NIF authorizes the company to proceed with registration, open bank accounts and enter into pre-registration contracts.
required_dossiers: First copy of the escritura de constitución
Modelo 036 - declaración censal with company data and administrators
Provisional NIF application form generated by the Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT issues an inquiry or rejects the census data, correct the Modelo 036 and resubmit with the required clarifications to the local AEAT Gestión Tributaria desk; any incorrect provisional NIF may be rectified after definitive inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Provincial Commercial Registry and publication in BORME
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is located, with publication in the Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil (BORME)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first authorized copy of the public deed together with the provisional NIF certificate and the ITPAJD model (Modelo 600) with the Registrar; the Registrar examines the legality and formal validity of the deed; upon approval, the registration is effected and the company acquires full legal personality; the registration is then published in BORME as a notice of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Primera copia autorizada de la escritura de constitución
Certificado del NIF provisional
Modelo 600 - autoliquidación del Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados (when due)
Bank certificate of capital deposit
Negative name certificate and provisional NIF certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar suspends or refuses the inscription due to a defect of form or legality, the Notary or the interested parties may cure the defect and resubmit the deed within the granted period; a final refusal may be appealed before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública, and ultimately before the contentious-administrative courts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation formalities: definitive NIF, legalization of corporate books and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Registro Mercantil Provincial; Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the inscripción is granted, the company obtains the definitive NIF issued by AEAT and updates the census record via Modelo 036; open and present the corporate books (minutes book, partners register, and capital variation book, plus annual accounts book if applicable) for legalization at the Commercial Registry; register the company and its administrators with TGSS as a new employer (código de cuenta de cotización) using the RED system; complete the municipal communication if the licensed activity is already initiated.
required_dossiers: Registration certificate issued by the Registro Mercantil
Definitive NIF certificate from AEAT
Modelo 036 census update
Corporate books (libro de actas, libro registro de socios) for legalization
TA.6 and TA.7 Social Security registration forms
Company bank account details and corporate address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the definitive NIF data conflicts with the provisional certificate, apply for a rectification at the AEAT office of origin; corporate books rejected for formal defects may be rebound and re-presented; employer registration issues at TGSS are cured by correcting the RED transmission and resubmitting the forms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal operating license and industrial installation authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento of the municipality where the production plant is located (Concejalía de Urbanismo y Licencias), with intervention of the competent Consejería of the autonomous community
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for the municipal license of classified activity (licencia de actividad clasificada) or, where the local ordinance allows, a prior communication of activity start, attaching the technical project of the factory, the fire safety certification, the simplified environmental assessment resolution, and the wastewater discharge authorization; after the municipal technical inspection, obtain the final operating permit and the first occupation certificate before commencing production.
required_dossiers: Formal application for licencia de actividad / declaración responsable de inicio de actividad
Technical project of the industrial installation signed by a competent technician
Fire safety project and certificate issued by the OCA (Organismo de Control Autorizado)
Simplified environmental impact assessment resolution when applicable under Ley 21/2013
Wastewater discharge authorization from the municipality or the hydrographic authority
CE declaration of conformity for manufacturing machinery
First occupation certificate issued by the municipal technical services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal license is denied or administrative silence produces a negative act, the company may cure the environmental or technical deficiencies and resubmit a corrected application; a denial may be appealed before the municipal plenary or the competent regional body, and ultimately before the contentious-administrative jurisdiction; positive silence applies only where the local ordinance expressly establishes it.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Agencia Española de Medicamentos y Productos Sanitarios (AEMPS) as the Spanish competent authority for medical devices under Regulation (EU) 2017/745; the industrial installation is supervised by the Consejería competente in industry and environment of the autonomous community and by the municipal Ayuntamiento
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro de fabricante de productos sanitarios and Declaración de Conformidad UE / CE marking for sterile examination gloves (Class IIa under Annex VIII of Regulation (EU) 2017/745) with conformity assessment by a Notified Body, together with the municipal Licencia de Actividad y Apertura of the industrial facility

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITECO) - Dirección General de Calidad y Evaluación Ambiental, coordinated with the environmental Consejería of the competent autonomous community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Simplificada under Article 7.2 and Annex II of Ley 21/2013, de 9 de diciembre, de evaluación ambiental, applicable to chemical and industrial installations; a full Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Ordinaria (Annex I) is only triggered when plant capacity or solvent/chemical thresholds exceed the statutory limits, in which case an Autorización Ambiental Integrada or Unificada must also be obtained
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Ley 7/2022, de 8 de abril, de residuos y suelos contaminados; wastewater discharge limits under Real Decreto 817/2015 and the municipal sewage by-law, typically BOD5 40 mg/L, COD 160 mg/L, TSS 60 mg/L with pH 6-9; fugitive VOC and solvent management per Real Decreto 117/2003 (compound limits for dipping facilities); application of Best Available Techniques for the manufacture of rubber and nitrile dipped products under the industrial emissions framework transposing Directive 2010/75/EU; waste latex solids and curing chemicals must be classified and managed through an authorized waste handler with traceability records.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate (certificado de protección contra incendios) for the industrial building issued by an authorized control body in accordance with Real Decreto 513/2017 on fire installations; certificate of first occupation verifying structural load and electric installation; workplace risk prevention plan under Ley 31/1995 with compliance to Real Decreto 486/1997 on workplace conditions and Real Decreto 374/2001 on chemical agents; technical documentation from INSST on worker exposure to nitrile solvents and airborne particulates; emergency evacuation plan, annual inspection of extinguishing equipment, and safety signaling in accordance with the applicable Spanish and EU standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); official online portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT — https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The foreign shareholders incorporate the SL before a Spanish notary and register it at the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil). The SL then must apply to AEAT for its definitive tax identification number (NIF) by filing the official census declaration (Form 036) within six months of obtaining the provisional NIF at incorporation. The same Form 036 simultaneously registers the company in the Spanish VAT census (Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores) and yields the Spanish IVA identification number, which is the NIF with the ES prefix for intra-EU transactions. Non-resident shareholders without a permanent establishment in Spain obtain only a non-resident NIF (Form 030) where needed for withholding or Spanish VAT obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — an SL is a separate corporate taxpayer subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) on its worldwide income; it is not eligible for any pass-through tax classification and does not qualify for transparent treatment under Spanish domestic law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or U.S.-style entity classification elections are available. Elective Spanish regimes applicable to an SL include: (i) the reduced 15% Corporate Income Tax rate for newly constituted entities engaging in an economic activity in their first two tax periods (Art. 29.1 Ley 27/2014, LIS); (ii) fiscal consolidation for qualifying groups where the parent holds at least 75% directly or indirectly in the SL (50% for listed companies), under Arts. 62–96 LIS; (iii) the ETVE holding-company regime election for Spanish-resident entities whose main purpose is the management of foreign shareholdings; (iv) the optional cash-basis VAT scheme (Criterio de Caja) for operators whose annual turnover is below EUR 2,000,000. Hybrid mismatch rules transposing ATAD (Law 4/2019) are mandatory and non-elective.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), governed by Law 37/1992, Royal Decree 1624/1992, and aligned with Council Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by AEAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR — Spain imposes no general de minimis turnover threshold: any person habitually supplying taxable goods or services in the course of business must register as an IVA operator before commencing activity. The only contextual thresholds are (i) EUR 10,000 in annual cross-border intra-EU distance sales of goods triggering Spanish VAT obligations, and (ii) EUR 2,000,000 in turnover for eligibility for the optional cash-basis VAT scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured B2B e-invoicing applies under Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece): suppliers must issue electronic invoices in the accredited interoperable Facturae XML profile through certified private platforms or the AEAT facade, and recipients must be able to receive such invoices. The Veri*factu regime (Royal Decree 1007/2023) requires business software in cash-handling activities to create a hash-chained record of transactional invoices accessible to AEAT on demand, with QR-code or Digital Identification control; there is no continuous real-time VAT fiscal clearance for ordinary B2B exports, but customs movements require electronic lodging in the Spanish Automated Export System (AES) and clearance must be evidenced by the Movement Reference Number (MRN).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: supplies of tangible personal property, including sterile examination nitrile gloves, physically dispatched or transported by the seller, the non-EU purchaser, or a carrier from Spanish customs territory to a non-EU destination qualify for VAT exemption with deduction of input VAT (effective 0%) under Art. 21 of Law 37/1992, provided the goods depart the EU within the statutory export time window, generally evidenced within three months of dispatch, and within 90 days where the shipment control procedure is used. Services: B2B services rendered to non-EU entrepreneurs fall outside the taxable scope of Spanish VAT under the place-of-supply rules of Art. 69 LIVA and are therefore subject to effective 0% Spanish taxation, with input VAT recovered through the deduction or refund channels.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Single Administrative Document (DUA) / Spanish Customs Export Declaration lodged and validated in the AES with an issued Movement Reference Number (MRN).
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list containing ISIC 3250 product codes, description of the sterile synthetic nitrile gloves, batch numbers, quantities, and Incoterms.
Transport document — Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note — evidencing physical dispatch from Spanish customs territory to the final non-EU destination.
The salida certificate (certificado de salida) or other electronic customs proof confirming that the goods physically departed the EU customs territory.
Bank payment evidence via the mandated payment rails (SWIFT LC or TT Wire) demonstrating receipt of export proceeds, including the inward remittance reference.
Where preferential origin is claimed, the Certificate of Origin (EUR.1 or Form A), together with any mandatory sanitary or CE compliance certificates required for medical device PPE export clearance.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may deny the zero-rating claim where export documentation is missing, materially defective, or untimely, and will re-assess the supply at the standard 21% VAT rate with late-payment interest. The four-year statute of limitation allows retrospective clawback of previously zero-rated or refunded VAT. Administrative penalties under Arts. 191–193 LGT range from 50% to 150% of the tax loss, with the highest range applied where the false export documentation derives from concealment or simulated operations. Where the intentionally concealed VAT exceeds EUR 120,000 in one tax period, or EUR 120,000 over four years, criminal tax fraud liability arises under Arts. 305–305 bis of the Criminal Code, and the legal representatives, directors, and customs-declaring brokers may incur joint and several liability in addition to public publication of the sanction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), functioning as the Spanish national central bank and banking supervisor, together with the Dirección General de Transacciones y Operaciones Exteriores (DGTOE) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business, which administers Spanish foreign exchange, foreign investment and balance-of-payments reporting under the Royal Decree 1816/1991 and its subsequent amendments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a full member of the European Union and the euro area. The euro is freely convertible, and Spain applies the EU principle of unrestricted movement of capital. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully liberalised for residents and non-residents. Profit remittances from a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) may be freely repatriated after corporate income tax compliance, subject only to standard withholding on dividends for non-resident shareholders, anti-money laundering due diligence by the paying bank, and statistical declaration to the DGTOE where thresholds apply. The manufacture and export of sterile examination nitrile gloves (ISIC 3250 / NAICS 339113) is not subject to any sectoral exchange restriction. Spanish banks generally convert EUR/USD and other major currencies at market rates, but availability for exotic currencies may be more limited.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no mandatory export-proceeds surrender rules in Spain. Exporters are not required to convert foreign-currency receipts into EUR nor to repatriate them within a specified statutory timeline. Export receipts may be held in foreign currency, converted freely, or used directly to pay foreign suppliers, subject to internal corporate treasury policy and Spanish balance-of-payments reporting obligations. Under Spanish foreign exchange regulations, export and import transactions above the applicable reporting threshold (currently EUR 1.25 million or its equivalent for annual aggregate settlements, with certain statistical forms such as D-6 and continuous monthly reporting) must be declared to the DGTOE for statistical purposes. The declaration is informational only and does not constitute an exchange-control requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for operational Euro-denominated collections and outbound wires, but Low for serving as the primary capital-escrow depository. A Spanish SL may lawfully use EEA-authorised e-money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions under the E-Money Directive and PSD2, provided the institution holds a valid authorisation in an EU/EEA member state or has been passported into Spain. Cross-border EMIs such as Wise Business, Payoneer, and Airwallex can be used for trade settlements, supplier disbursements, and foreign-currency conversion, but they are generally not accepted by Spanish notaries for the certification of capital contributions in an SL. The constitutional deed for the SL requires a bank certificate of capital deposit issued by a credit institution located in the EU/EEA that is a bank, not merely an EMI. Legal constraints include: EMI safeguarding requirements, restrictions on providing credit, data residency and AML/CFT obligations, and the need for the EMI's Spanish or passporting licence to be verified before account opening.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish banks generally require at least one commercial director or authorised signatory to attend an in-person identity verification interview, or a notarised power of attorney combined with video-identification where the bank's internal policy permits remote onboarding. For a non-resident shareholder opening an SL bank account, the bank will normally request the physical presence of the appointed managing director, or a duly appointed representative holding a notarised and legalised (Apostille) power of attorney. Remote onboarding is possible under the Seventh Anti-Money Laundering Directive and Spanish AML Law 10/2010 where the bank performs enhanced due diligence through geolocation, biometric verification, certified copies, and independent verification of directors, but many tier-one banks still require an initial physical meeting or a visit to a local branch for high-risk jurisdictions. For this standard-risk medical PPE exporter, timely onboarding is best achieved through an initial physical visit to Madrid or Barcelona, supported by a complete corporate statutory dossier.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders and foreign beneficial owners with no prior EU banking footprint attracting enhanced due diligence and possible rejection if UBO documentation is incomplete or not apostilled.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified copy of the constitutional deed (escritura pública) registered in the Mercantile Registry, the NIF (CIF) tax certificate, a current certificate of the beneficial ownership registry (Registro de Titularidades Reales), apostilled and legalised passport copies of all direct and indirect shareholders, a clear corporate organigram, and bank references from the home jurisdiction. For Spanish SLs, the initial EUR 3,000 (or agreed) capital contribution certificate issued by the Spanish bank is also mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected pattern of high volumes of cross-border TT/LC transactions, or frequent payments to third-party suppliers in multiple jurisdictions, which may be flagged as a mismatch against the declared, low-risk medical PPE activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a detailed business plan and treasury forecast showing the trade flow: selected supplier invoices, pro-forma invoices, purchase orders, contracts with overseas distributors, ISO 13485 and CE-marking certificates, EORI number, and the ISIC/NAICS classification of the product. Maintain a historical ledger of past export transactions, a documented AML/CFT risk assessment, and clear internal controls on third-party payment approvals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from jurisdictions with enhanced risk, including Latin American and Middle Eastern markets that the Spain-Latin America trade corridor may target, triggering temporary freezes and request for comprehensive end-to-end beneficial owner verification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Build and present the complete end-to-end transaction chain: contract in Spanish/English, market registration certificate for the glove product, commercial licence for imported medical devices, UNSPSC or HS code (e.g., 3926.20 or 4015.19 depending on material), import licences from the destination country, sanctions screening evidence for all counterparties, and an explanation of freight, insurance, and each payment purpose code. If the counterparty has no credit institution rating, add invoices from freight forwarders and logistics providers to substantiate the physical trade.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For an SL capital contribution, funds must be transferred by Swift MT103 or through an express domestic/SEPA transfer from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Spanish SL's new bank account, referencing the notarial deed of incorporation or capital increase, the shareholder's name, and the capital subscription records. The bank must issue a certificate of deposit confirming receipt of the statutory capital (desembolso) which the notary attaches to the deed. For non-EU foreign investment, after the notarial deed is granted, the SL (or its notary) must file the annual or transactional foreign-investment declaration with the DGTOE under Royal Decree 571/2020. The recommended wire purpose code is 'GITI/CIP' (Cross-Border Capital Injection / Foreign Direct Investment) using ISO 20022 purpose codes such as 'FDI1' or 'CAPD', with the narrative clearly stating 'Direct foreign investment in ordinary capital of Spanish SL'. The bank may request a copy of the signed share subscription, passport of the transferor, and source-of-funds evidence; the wire should originate only from the shareholder's own bank account and not a third-party pooling account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements related to nitrile glove production inputs and export logistics, Spanish SLs use: (i) the SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) immediate rail for EUR payments to EU suppliers; (ii) SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfers for non-EUR or non-EU payments, with purpose codes such as 'TRADE' / 'ADVA' for advance payments, and reference to the underlying commercial invoice; (iii) SWIFT MT700 commercial letters of credit for high-value or high-risk jurisdictions, where the Spanish issuing bank adds an irrevocable deferred-payment LC; and (iv) documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for established buyer relationships. Each outbound payment must be supported by the supplier invoice, purchase order, transport documents or Bill of Lading where dispatched, and the relevant DGTOE reporting if the cumulative transaction exceeds EUR 1.25 million. No separate central bank authorisation is required, but the bank must screen counterparties for EU sanctions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Contractual forward ( outright EUR/USD FX forward with a Spanish credit institution or EU-licensed investment firm)
Rolling or window forward contracts for EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL or EUR/CLP where the underlying Latin American trade receivable/payable is demonstrated
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) offered by Spanish banks for illiquid emerging-market currencies that are not freely transferable or where deliverability is limited
FX swaps (short-dated exchange of EUR and foreign currency with a simultaneous reversal)
Cross-currency swaps involving EUR and USD/Latin American currencies for medium-term matching of cross-border cash flows
Plain-vanilla over-the-counter FX options (with premium payment) that are economically-linked to specific export invoices or capital flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Memoria Anual - Annual Accounts and Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 300000 EUR, potential administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of any change or annually if unchanged
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to 100000 EUR and possible company sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Modelo 347 - Annual Report on Transactions with Non-Residents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of 1000 EUR per omitted transaction, maximum 100000 EUR

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if net turnover exceeds 8000000 EUR, total assets exceed 4000000 EUR, or net equity exceeds 2000000 EUR
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General Contable) pursuant to Royal Decree 1514/2007

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of UBOs and beneficial ownership structure in the Registro Mercantil, with updates required within one month of changes

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly created Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada subject to activity conditions are taxed at a 15% rate on the first EUR 300,000 of taxable income and 20% on the remainder of taxable income in the first tax year in which they obtain a positive taxable base and in the following tax year. General IP royalties may benefit from the Spanish patent box exemption (50% exemption on eligible licensing income), and R&D tax credits of 25% for qualifying R&D expenditures and 42% for R&D investments in fixed assets are available. Tax losses have no expiration for carryforward purposes, although annual offset limits may apply according to turnover thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 rendered through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) Sede Electrónica; mandatory electronic filing using digital certificate, Cl@ve PIN, or authorized representative. Quarterly provisional tax payments are filed via Modelo 202.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual Modelo 200 return; Modelo 202 quarterly installment payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Modelo 200 annual return must be filed within 25 days after the six-month period following the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year entity, the deadline is 25 July of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Identification Number of the tax entity, legal form code, dominant group indicator, and main corporate identification data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies acting through a Spanish permanent establishment must obtain an NIF-N and include the branch's local tax identity; non-resident entities without a permanent establishment do not file Modelo 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Pre-tax accounting profit or loss of the Spanish company prepared under Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident with a permanent establishment, enter the accounting result derived from audio-separated Spanish-branch accounts; passive foreign income not attributable to the Spanish PE should be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments to accounting result to arrive at taxable base, including reversal of temporary differences, permanent adjustments, and prior-year tax loss offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs must apply the same adjustments as resident companies, but reconciliation should reflect only assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses economically connected to the Spanish PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after integration of qualifying capitalization reserve and compensation of prior tax losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Spanish PE, the taxable base is the net income effectively connected to the PE determined under Article 13 of the Non-Resident Income Tax Act; deductions such as the capitalization reserve require Spanish substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax rate applied to the taxable base: generally 25%; 15% for qualifying newly created entities within the limits explained above.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs generally use the same 25% statutory rate. Treaty nondiscrimination clauses do not ordinarily alter the rate, but income tax treaty rules may affect the computation of business profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Result of applying the tax rate to the taxable base before deductions, bonuses, and double-taxation relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs include credits for taxes withheld at source in Spain and foreign income taxes attributable to the PE when they qualify for double-taxation relief under the relevant tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D credit, patent box, environmental investment credit, export credit, and other legally recognized tax incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only incentives available to a Spanish PE under domestic law may be claimed; they must be substantiated by Spanish bookkeeping and by the PE's actual execution of the qualifying activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax result after offsetting Modelo 202 installment payments, withholding taxes, and other payments on account made during the tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs settle any residual balance through the annual Modelo 200 and may not offset taxes already paid abroad except where permitted by the applicable DTA and domestic double-tax relief provisions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Modelo 200 without prior AEAT demand is subject to a graduated surcharge under Article 27 LGT: 5% within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months, and 20% after twelve months, plus late-payment interest. If the AEAT formally requires the return, the penalty may be a proportional fine of 50% to 150% of the tax loss. Employer withholding and quarterly Modelo 202 failures attract additional fixed penalties and daily surcharges. Where deliberate evasion exceeds EUR 120,000 in any tax period, criminal tax fraud proceedings may be instituted.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 24% general rate under Spanish Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) for dividends paid to non-residents without a permanent establishment in Spain; 19% for EU/EEA residents under the general EU/EEA rule where not exempted; 0% for qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive dividends, subject to holding and substance conditions; treaty rates may reduce the rate to 0%, 5%, or 10% depending on the relevant double-taxation agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder claiming DTA relief must: (1) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its jurisdiction of fiscal residence, (2) deliver the certificate to the Spanish paying entity before the dividend payment is made so that the payer may apply the reduced or zero treaty rate, (3) submit a beneficial ownership declaration, and (4) if withholding was applied at the statutory rate, file Modelo 210 with the AEAT within four years of the payment to claim a refund. For EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief, the qualifying EU parent must also provide a residence certificate and evidence of the required direct shareholding percentage and minimum holding period, usually at least 25% and one year of continuous holding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid by a Spanish SL for IP rights to a non-resident are subject to a 24% IRNR domestic withholding rate unless reduced by a DTA (commonly 5% to 10%) or eliminated by the EU Interest and Royalties Directive when the beneficial owner is a qualifying EU affiliate. Interest paid to a non-resident is also ordinarily subject to a 24% domestic IRNR withholding rate, with treaty rates typically ranging from 0% to 10%; interest paid to EU credit institutions may enjoy statutory exemptions, and interest under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive may be subject to 0% withholding if the relevant holding and substance conditions are met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not maintain offshore-style Economic Substance Regulations comparable to low-tax jurisdictions. However, Spanish tax law imposes a real economic substance doctrine through Article 15 of the General Tax Law (simulation), Article 13 of the Corporate Income Tax Act (attribution of dependent enterprise profits to a PE), the controlled foreign company regime, and the OECD Treaty Abuse Limitation / Principal Purpose Test. A Spanish SL lacking physical premises, qualified personnel, management decision-making, or business risk in Spain may be recharacterized as a shell entity, with consequent denial of treaty benefits, disregarding of artificial intercompany arrangements, and reallocation of business profits to the real economic owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and intentional omission of income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsification of invoices, hidden bank accounts, deliberate non-declaration of Spain-source sales, fictitious expenses connected to nitrile glove procurement, and concealment of beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Proportional tax penalty between 50% and 150% of the evaded tax amount plus late-payment interest. Criminal tax fraud is triggered when defrauded tax amounts exceed EUR 120,000 per tax period, punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who ordered or participated in the infringement are jointly and severally liable for the defrauded tax and penalties; criminal conviction may add travel bans, seizure of personal assets, disqualification from public contracts, and custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial shell company and simulation of corporate activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Spanish SL established solely to invoice distributions or royalties without employees, local office, business purpose, or risk management; decision-making conducted entirely outside Spain; nominee arrangements with no operative capacity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under Article 15 LGT as simulated transactions, denial of treaty benefits, CFC attribution of passive income to the Spanish entity, 25% corporate income tax assessment plus penalties, and financial interst on unpaid tax. Qualified offshore shell companies may also be reached under EU anti-tax-avoidance directives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors' personal liability may arise under the 'levantamiento del velo' doctrine, including joint liability for taxes and penalties, civil restitution, prohibition on leaving Spanish territory pending proceedings, and, in cases of fraud, criminal liability for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing mispricing and inadequate documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany payments for management fees, royalty-free transfer of sterilization technology, excessive commissions to foreign distributors, or inadequate profit margin on high-speed dipping glove production when compared to arm's length independent transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may adjust the transaction to arm's length, increasing Spanish taxable base, impose a 15% penalty on the amount of the secondary adjustment, apply late-payment interest, and levy an additional 50% to 150% proportional penalty if the TP adjustment arises from intentional falsity or manipulation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or knowingly participated in the transfer pricing mispricing are jointly and severally liable for the additional tax, penalties, and interest; may also be held personally liable for damages to the company and charged with tax fraud if the adjustment reveals criminal culpability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, cash-structuring, and cross-border payment red flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Unusual TT wire and Swift LC payments routed through high-risk jurisdictions, repeated cash payments just below reporting thresholds, mismatched beneficial ownership in corporate registries, or failure to conduct KYC/CDD on clients purchasing sterile nitrile gloves through intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violations of Law 10/2010 on prevention of money laundering can result in administrative fines from EUR 60,000 to EUR 5,000,000 for serious or very serious infringements, and may include temporary closure of the business and loss of operating licenses. Criminal money laundering charges can be pursued if proceeds arise from predicate crime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives and AML compliance officers may be personally fined, prohibited from management roles, ordered to travel bans, and, where criminal laundering is proven, subjected to imprisonment. The corporate veil is pierced where the company was used as a mere instrument to execute fraudulent transactions.
